_comment: R24 vertical bootstrap suite. Deliberately small; all cases resolved against EXISTING spec/*/*.yaml files (none invented). See docs/design/r24-cpp-host-preflight.md section 6. Run via: python -m tools.spec_runner --host '<cpp-adapter-cmd>' --evidence <path> (the runner has no case-filter flag, so a genia-cpp CI job stages only these files into a temp spec/ tree, or filters the --evidence output post-hoc).
expansion_policy: Expansion beyond this list is a per-slice decision made by the E24 implementation ticket introducing the new capability or behavior (see docs/strategy/roadmap/e24-issue-sequence.md), never a blanket 'add more cases' change.
A category may not be widened, and a new category may not be added, without the corresponding capability already being declared in docs/design/r24/capability-floor.json.
Every case added to this file must already exist in genia-2026's spec/ tree at the pinned contract revision; genia-cpp must never invent its own case files as a substitute.
This file is updated in the same PR that changes genia-cpp's declared capability set, so the two never drift apart.

corrections.change: Removed spec/eval/pattern-literal-string.yaml from the 'literals' category. That case requires function definitions, full pattern/case dispatch, and string-literal support to execute (category: eval) -- none of which match this category's own 'capability: parser' tag, and all of which are out of E24-2's declared scope (pattern/case dispatch is separately evidenced by the pattern_case_dispatch category and is E24-4's scope; string-literal parsing is E24-3's scope per docs/strategy/roadmap/e24-issue-sequence.md). No replacement case exists yet under spec/parse/ for bare string-literal parsing; add one as part of E24-3 if that category needs widening then. Also corrected total_case_count, which was already stale before this fix (documented as 19 while the categories actually summed to 20); the true post-fix sum is 19.

Replaced spec/eval/pattern-list-exact.yaml in 'list_construction_and_use' with the new spec/eval/list-literal-construction-and-equality.yaml: the original case required a full function definition with multi-clause pattern dispatch (list-destructure clause + wildcard fallback), which is E24-4's pattern_case_dispatch scope (already separately evidenced by pattern-map-partial.yaml), not list construction/use. Replaced spec/eval/map-put-replace-existing-key-preserves-order.yaml in 'ordered_map_behavior' with the new spec/eval/map-put-replace-existing-key-preserves-order-via-items.yaml: the original case's use of map_keys pulls in map/map_acc (tuple patterns, list rest-patterns, recursion, apply_raw), also E24-4-scope machinery; the replacement proves the identical R17 replace-preserves-order property via map_items (a trivial native-delegation prelude wrapper, like the category's other pinned case) instead. Also replaced both cases in 'equality_and_legal_key_behavior': spec/eval/r18-equality-structural-contents.yaml and spec/eval/r18-map-key-equivalence-is-equality.yaml each required Decimal literals (1.0, 0.0, -0.0), which is E24-7's exact-numeric-model scope, and the former also required Option values (some(...)), E24-4's outcome_values scope; replaced with spec/eval/r18-structural-equality-bytes-and-lists.yaml and spec/eval/r18-legal-key-kind-separation-integer-string.yaml, proving the identical structural-equality and legal-key-kind-separation properties using only Bytes/List/Integer/Boolean/String values. All four new cases were verified against the Python reference host via the in-process spec_runner (744 total, 744 passed, 0 failed) before being pinned here.

Replaced spec/eval/r20-cross-module-order-independence.yaml in 'open_functions_r20' with spec/eval/r20-gcd-repeated-clauses.yaml. The original case uses the multi-file 'modules: {entry, files: [...]}' test-harness shape and its own 'requires:' block lists multi_file_eval alongside open_functions; docs/design/r24/capability-floor.json explicitly places multi_file_eval under generic_manifest_optional_capabilities_explicitly_out_of_r24_scope, and its claim_rules forbid any R24 completion evidence depending on an out-of-scope capability. Every spec/eval/r20-cross-module-*.yaml case uses the same multi-file harness (cross-module R20 semantics are inherently multi-file in the existing shared spec corpus), so no single-file substitute exists that still exercises cross-module contribution/selection specifically. The replacement is single-file and exercises R20's other Includes item instead (local grouped/repeated open-function clauses): it is the repeated-top-level-clause sibling spelling of the category's other pinned case (grouped-clause spelling), proving the same 'clauses for one interface accumulate/dispatch identically regardless of spelling' property. Verified against the Python reference host directly (PYTHONPATH=src python3 src/genia/interpreter.py -c '...') before being pinned here: both cases print 6, matching each case's expected.stdout. E24-6's open_functions capability declaration must stay 'partial' (not 'supported') until cross-module evidence becomes achievable, since multi_file_eval remains out of R24 scope. NOTE: this closing statement about 'partial' was corrected by #973 below -- see that entry.

Corrects #971's closing statement above, which asserted genia-cpp must declare open_functions 'partial' (not 'supported'). tools/spec_runner/capabilities.py's case_is_applicable gate only attempts a case whose 'requires' list names open_functions when the host declares open_functions exactly 'supported' -- 'partial' grants zero evidence credit (the module's own docstring: 'partial-capability satisfaction, if ever added, is a separate contract decision, not an E16-3 default'). Since both cases #971 pinned for 'open_functions_r20' carry 'requires: [open_functions]', #971's guidance would have made those two pinned cases permanently un-runnable -- the opposite of the point of pinning them. Corrected guidance: genia-cpp should declare open_functions 'supported', matching the same precedent already used for its parser/ast_lowering/cli_command_mode/cli_file_mode capabilities (declaring 'supported' means 'implements enough to meaningfully attempt gated cases,' not '100% of the capability's surface' -- per-case pass/fail/unsupported is still decided independently for every case). This is not a claim that cross-module extend/use, the R20 diagnostic family, or bare varargs patterns are implemented; those remain genuinely unsupported per-case, or gated out entirely by the separate multi_file_eval requirement on every cross-module case. Verified empirically against genia-cpp's actual E24-6 implementation: declaring open_functions supported and running the full 744-case corpus produces failed=0, crash=0. No case files or total_case_count change -- documentation/guidance correction only.
